ESCAPE SPELLING: these strings hold the JSON escape  (one backslash), which parses to the real ESC byte; pexpect sends it raw, and Python re matches the raw byte too, so the same spelling serves expects and sends. A double backslash would parse to the SIX-CHARACTER TEXT : re still converts it in a pattern, but a send would write the literal text and the app would never see the arrow. Run at 120x30 for headroom. LOADABLE EXPORT REQUIRED: the driver must start the app in a fresh tempdir holding a synthesized `mydata~1784667002819/json/chat_history.json` (two conversations, one titled). The t step's whole evidence is the disabled chip at the end: the picker must have LOADED (the load defaults the selection to every conversation), and the t must have deselected it. From a dir with no export the picker holds the load's refusal, the selection is empty anyway, and the tooltip would render without any t having been pressed. STALE-FRAME TRAP: every expect matches the OLDEST unconsumed bytes in the driver's buffer, so a pattern drawn several frames back matches instantly even while the app has moved on; the steps below expect fresh evidence (a hint bar or tooltip only the keypress in question draws) wherever a step's SEND depends on the app's state.

HOW TO GATE THIS RUN: require the printed final line to be exactly EXIT:0 AND stderr to contain no '[step N] TIMEOUT'. Do NOT gate on tui-drive.py's own process exit code - it returns `child.exitstatus or 0`, and a timed-out step only breaks the loop, so a failed flow and an app that never quit both yield process rc 0.
